chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about two men who jointly have a female slave. One of them frees his half, and the slave says to the one who did not free his half, “I do not want you to appraise me; leave me as I am, and I will serve you,” while he wanted to marry the other half of her.

He عليه السلام said: “It is not proper for him to do that, for a woman cannot have two private parts. Nor is it proper for him to keep her in service; rather, he should appraise her and have her work to pay off the remaining share.”

key_terms.الْأَمَةُ: a female slave jointly owned in this case
key_terms.فَرْجَانِ: two private parts; used here to negate dual legal status
key_terms.فَيُعْتِقُ: he emancipates or frees from slavery
key_terms.يَسْتَسْعِيهَا: to require her to work toward paying off the remaining amount
key_terms.يَسْتَنْكِحَ: to marry or seek conjugal relation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one co-owner frees his share of a female slave and the other wants to marry or keep using her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a jointly owned female slave when one partner emancipates his share. The Imam عليه السلام forbids combining marital access with partial ownership and also forbids continuing to use her merely as a servant in that state; instead, her value is to be assessed and she is to work toward settling the remaining share.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3438 - Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about two men who jointly own a female slave. One of them frees his half, and the slave says to the one who did not free his half, "I do not want to be valued; leave me as I am, and I will continue serving you."
Meanwhile, the owner intends to marry the other half of her.
Imam (as) said: "He should not do that, for a woman cannot have two private parts. Nor should he use her for service. Instead, he must value her and let her work to pay off the remaining portion."
